## API Reference

## app methods

All methods return `Promise<void>` unless noted.

### Interaction

| Method               | Signature                  | Description                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tap`                | `(selector, opts?)`        | Tap an element matching the selector                                                                               |
| `tapXY`              | `(x, y)`                   | Tap at absolute screen coordinates                                                                                 |
| `doubleTap`          | `(selector, opts?)`        | Double-tap an element                                                                                              |
| `longPress`          | `(selector, opts?)`        | Long-press an element                                                                                              |
| `longPressXY`        | `(x, y, opts?)`            | Long-press at coordinates                                                                                          |
| `inputText`          | `(text)`                   | Type text into the focused element                                                                                 |
| `fill`               | `(selector, value, opts?)` | Focus, clear, and fill an input in one round trip on a DOM channel; falls back to `tap` + `inputText` on native UI |
| `pressKey`           | `(key)`                    | Press a named key                                                                                                  |
| `hideKeyboard`       | `()`                       | Dismiss the software keyboard                                                                                      |
| `dismissKeyboard`    | `(opts?)`                  | Platform-aware keyboard dismissal                                                                                  |
| `swipe`              | `(direction, opts?)`       | Swipe in a direction                                                                                               |
| `scroll`             | `(direction)`              | Scroll in a direction                                                                                              |
| `scrollUntilVisible` | `(selector, opts?)`        | Scroll until the element is visible                                                                                |
| `backUntilVisible`   | `(selector, opts?)`        | Go back until the element is visible                                                                               |

Direction: `"up" | "down" | "left" | "right"`

### App lifecycle

| Method       | Signature          | Description                       |
| ------------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `launch`     | `(opts?)`          | Launch the app                    |
| `stop`       | `()`               | Stop the app                      |
| `kill`       | `()`               | Force-kill the app                |
| `clearState` | `()`               | Clear app data/state              |
| `openLink`   | `(url)`            | Open a URL or deep link           |
| `openStory`  | `(storyId, opts?)` | Open a Storybook story (web only) |
| `back`       | `()`               | Browser back or Android back      |

### Utilities

| Method           | Signature                   | Description                                               |
| ---------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `takeScreenshot` | `(name?)`                   | `Promise<Uint8Array>` — capture the current screen        |
| `getText`        | `(selector, opts?)`         | `Promise<string>` — read an element's text                |
| `getAttribute`   | `(selector, name, opts?)`   | `Promise<string \| null>` — read an attribute             |
| `isVisible`      | `(selector, { timeout? }?)` | `Promise<boolean>` — check visibility without throwing    |
| `isEnabled`      | `(selector, opts?)`         | `Promise<boolean>` — check enabled state without throwing |
| `evaluate`       | `(fn \| string, ...args)`   | Run JavaScript in the page                                |

### Web-first bridge and browser-only helpers

| Method                                                                             | Signature            | Description                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `waitForIdle`                                                                      | `(opts?)`            | Wait for network, animations, and renders to settle (needs `spana-bridge`)        |
| `setStorage`                                                                       | `(entries)`          | Inject storage / auth state through the DOM bridge                                |
| `clearStorage`                                                                     | `(opts?)`            | Clear localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, IndexedDB, and Capacitor Preferences |
| `resetFast`                                                                        | `()`                 | Clear storage through the bridge and reload                                       |
| `getPage`                                                                          | `()`                 | Return the underlying page object (web)                                           |
| `enableVirtualAuthenticator`                                                       | `(opts?)`            | `Promise<string>` — add a WebAuthn virtual authenticator                          |
| `getVirtualCredentials` / `clearVirtualCredentials` / `removeVirtualAuthenticator` | `(authenticatorId?)` | Manage virtual WebAuthn credentials                                               |

Browser, network, tab, WebView-context, and gesture helpers (`mockNetwork`, `newTab`, `switchToWebView`, `pinch`, and more) use the same signatures as the [Agent API](/reference/agent-api/) session methods.

## expect methods

```ts
expect(selector: Selector): PromiseExpectation
```

| Method                                                  | Signature                                            | Description                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `toBeVisible`                                           | `(opts?)`                                            | Assert element is present and visible     |
| `toBeHidden`                                            | `(opts?)`                                            | Assert element is absent or not visible   |
| `toHaveText`                                            | `(expected, opts?)`                                  | Assert element text equals `expected`     |
| `toContainText`                                         | `(expected, opts?)`                                  | Assert element text contains `expected`   |
| `toMatchText`                                           | `(pattern, opts?)`                                   | Assert element text matches a `RegExp`    |
| `toHaveValue`                                           | `(expected, opts?)`                                  | Assert an input value                     |
| `toHaveAttribute`                                       | `(name, value?, opts?)`                              | Assert an attribute exists or has a value |
| `toBeEnabled` / `toBeDisabled`                          | `(opts?)`                                            | Assert enabled state                      |
| `toMatchScreenshot`                                     | `(name, { threshold?, maxDiffPixelRatio?, mask? }?)` | Visual regression against a baseline      |
| `toPassAccessibilityAudit`                              | `({ severity?, rules?, exclude? }?)`                 | Run an accessibility audit                |
| `toHaveAccessibilityLabel`                              | `(expected?)`                                        | Assert an accessibility label             |
| `toBeFocusable` / `toHaveRole` / `toHaveMinTouchTarget` | `()` / `(role)` / `(size?)`                          | Accessibility checks                      |

## Selectors

| Type                 | Example                           | Notes                                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `string`             | `"Sign In"`                       | Shorthand text match (case-insensitive, partial)          |
| `testID`             | `{ testID: "login-btn" }`         | `data-testid` / `accessibilityIdentifier` / `resource-id` |
| `text`               | `{ text: "Sign In" }`             | Visible label, case-insensitive partial match             |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `{ accessibilityLabel: "Close" }` | OS accessibility label                                    |
| `point`              | `{ point: { x: 100, y: 200 } }`   | Absolute coordinates, last resort                         |

Add `systemUI: true` (or use the `systemUI(...)` helper) on `text` / `accessibilityLabel` selectors to target OS UI such as OAuth sheets and permission dialogs. Relative selectors (`{ selector, below?, above?, leftOf?, rightOf?, childOf? }`) are also accepted.

## WaitOptions

Accepted by all selector-based `app` methods and all `expect` methods.

```ts
interface WaitOptions {
  timeout?: number; // ms, default 5000
  pollInterval?: number; // ms, default 200
  settleTimeout?: number; // ms, default 0
  initialPollInterval?: number; // ms, default 50 (adaptive polling)
  tapMode?: "native" | "dom";
}
```

## FlowConfig

```ts
interface FlowConfig {
  tags?: string[];
  platforms?: Array<"web" | "android" | "ios" | "electron" | "electrobun">;
  timeout?: number;
  autoLaunch?: boolean; // default true
  launchOptions?: LaunchOptions;
  artifacts?: ArtifactConfig; // same shape as config `artifacts`
  defaults?: {
    /* per-flow timing overrides */
  };
  when?: WhenCondition;
}

interface LaunchOptions {
  clearState?: boolean;
  clearKeychain?: boolean;
  deepLink?: string;
  launchArguments?: Record<string, unknown>;

}
```

## defineConfig options

```ts
interface SpanaConfig {
  apps?: {

  flowDir?: string;

}
```

---

## Architecture Overview

spana uses a layered architecture where all logic lives in TypeScript on the host machine. Platform drivers are thin clients (HTTP for UiAutomator2/WebDriverAgent/Appium, CDP or Playwright for browsers and desktop webviews) with no embedded selector logic.

## High-level architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[flow files .flow.ts] --> B[CLI: spana test]
    B --> C[TestRunner / runner.ts]
    C --> D[PlatformOrchestrator]
    D --> E1[Web: Playwright, direct CDP, or Lightpanda]
    D --> E2[Android: UiAutomator2]
    D --> E3[iOS: WebDriverAgent]
    D --> E4[Electron / Electrobun]
    E1 --> F[Reporter]
    E2 --> F
    E3 --> F
    E4 --> F
    F --> G1[console]
    F --> G2[json]
    F --> G3[junit]
    F --> G4[html]
    F --> G5[allure / github]
```

By default, platforms run one after another so each runtime has exclusive access to its simulator, emulator, or browser. They run concurrently when you pass `--parallel`, `--workers`, or `--devices`, or set `parallelPlatforms: true` in config. Within a platform, flows run serially on one worker, or are pulled from a shared queue when the platform has several workers (see [Parallel execution](#parallel-execution)). Results are collected and passed to the configured reporter(s).

## Layered architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph User API
        A1["flow() — define test"]
        A2["app — launch, tap, swipe, type"]
        A3["expect — toBeVisible, toHaveText, toBeHidden"]
    end

    subgraph Smart Layer [Smart Layer — src/smart/]
        B1[coordinator.ts — action dispatch]
        B2[auto-wait.ts — poll until element appears]
        B3[element-matcher.ts — client-side tree search + centerOf]
    end

    subgraph Raw Driver [Raw Driver — src/drivers/raw-driver.ts]
        C[RawDriverService interface]
        C1[tapAtCoordinate / swipe / inputText]
        C2[dumpHierarchy — returns raw XML or JSON]
        C3[launchApp / stopApp / takeScreenshot]
    end

    subgraph Companion Drivers
        D1[playwright.ts / cdp-browser.ts — Playwright or direct CDP]
        D2[uiautomator2/driver.ts — HTTP to APK server]
        D3[wda/driver.ts — HTTP to XCTest runner]
    end

    subgraph Devices
        E1[Browser / Chromium]
        E2[Android emulator or device]
        E3[iOS simulator or device]
    end

    A2 --> B1
    A3 --> B1
    B1 --> B2
    B2 --> C2
    B2 --> B3
    B3 --> B1
    B1 --> C1
    C --> D1
    C --> D2
    C --> D3
    D1 --> E1
    D2 --> E2
    D3 --> E3
```

The Smart Layer resolves selectors to elements, derives center coordinates, then calls the thin `RawDriver` interface. The coordinate-level `RawDriver` methods know nothing about selectors. When a driver exposes an optional DOM channel (web drivers, or the in-app `spana-bridge` for webviews), the Smart Layer can resolve and act on selectors inside the page instead (`smart/channel-resolver.ts`).

## Element resolution flow

How `app.tap({ testID: "login" })` executes end-to-end:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Flow as flow.ts
    participant Coord as coordinator.ts
    participant Wait as auto-wait.ts
    participant Driver as RawDriverService
    participant Parser as platform parser
    participant Companion as companion server

    Flow->>Coord: tap({ testID: "login" })
    Coord->>Wait: waitForElement(selector)
    loop poll until found or timeout
        Wait->>Driver: dumpHierarchy()
        Driver->>Companion: HTTP GET /session/:id/source
        Companion-->>Driver: raw XML / JSON string
        Driver-->>Wait: RawHierarchy
        Wait->>Parser: parse(raw) -> Element tree
        Wait->>Wait: findElement(tree, { testID: "login" })
    end
    Wait-->>Coord: Element (with bounds)
    Coord->>Coord: centerOf(element) -> {x, y}
    Coord->>Driver: tapAtCoordinate(x, y)
    Driver->>Companion: HTTP POST /appium/gestures/click (Android) or /wda/tap (iOS)
```

The diagram shows the native (Android/iOS) path. The parser is platform-specific (XML for Android/iOS, JSON for web) but always produces the same unified `Element` tree shape. On the native path, all matching logic runs client-side in TypeScript.

## Parallel execution

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Flow Queue [Shared flow queue]
        Q1[flow 1]
        Q2[flow 2]
        Q3[flow 3]
        Q4[flow 4]
        Q5[flow 5]
    end

    subgraph Workers
        W1[Worker A — Pixel 7]
        W2[Worker B — Galaxy S23]
        W3[Worker C — iPhone 15 sim]
    end

    Q1 --> W1
    Q2 --> W2
    Q3 --> W3
    Q4 --> W1
    Q5 --> W2

    W1 --> R[Aggregated Results]
    W2 --> R
    W3 --> R
```

Workers share a single atomic index into the flow array. Because Bun is single-threaded, the increment is naturally safe with no mutex. A faster device finishes sooner and picks up the next flow immediately, draining the queue at the speed of the fastest workers. When a previous run recorded flow durations (`spana-output/.spana/last-run.json`), the queue is ordered longest-first.

For web, `--workers <n>` creates `n` isolated browser contexts spread across `ceil(n / execution.web.maxContextsPerBrowser)` browser processes (default: 1 context per browser for the `cdp` engine, 2 for `playwright`). Android and iOS get one worker per discovered device.

- `parallel.ts` — `runParallel()` launches all workers with `Promise.all`, each looping over the queue until exhausted.
- `orchestrator.ts` — `orchestrate()` runs each platform (single worker or `runParallel()` pool). Platforms run serially unless `parallelPlatforms` is enabled.
- `runtime/local.ts` — `buildWebRuntimePool()` builds the web worker pool.

## Agent workflow

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Agent] -->|spana selectors --platform android| B[Discover elements\nJSON list with suggestedSelector]
    B -->|generate flow code| C[Write flow.ts]
    C -->|spana validate| D[Validate schema\nno device needed]
    D -->|spana test --reporter json| E[Execute on device]
    E -->|read JSON errors| F[Fix and retry]
    F --> C
```

`session.ts` backs `spana hierarchy` and `spana selectors`. `Session.selectors()` dumps the element tree, flattens it, and returns only visible elements with a `testID`, `accessibilityLabel`, or `text` — each annotated with the best-priority selector to use in a flow file.

## Monorepo structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    Root[spana/]

    Root --> Packages[packages/]
    Root --> Apps[apps/]

    Packages --> PProvPkg[spana/ — core library and CLI]
    Packages --> Bridge[spana-bridge/ — in-app DOM bridge]
    Packages --> NativePkg[spana-native/ — Rust native accelerator]
    Packages --> Config[config/ — shared TS/lint config]
    Packages --> Env[env/ — environment helpers]
    Packages --> UI[ui/ — shared UI components]

    Apps --> Web[web/ — web app under test]
    Apps --> Native[native/ — React Native app under test]
    Apps --> TUI[tui/ — terminal UI]
    Apps --> Studio[studio/ — Spana Studio UI]
    Apps --> Docs[docs/]

    PProvPkg --> Src[src/]
    Src --> API[api/ — flow, app, expect user API]
    Src --> Core[core/ — engine, orchestrator, parallel, runner]
    Src --> Smart[smart/ — coordinator, auto-wait, element-matcher]
    Src --> Drivers[drivers/ — raw-driver interface + platform impls]
    Src --> Channels[channels/ — CDP, WebKit inspector, bridge DOM channels]
    Src --> Runtime[runtime/ — local, Appium, web engine selection]
    Src --> Cloud[cloud/ — BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, custom providers]
    Src --> Agent[agent/ — session.ts for agent/CLI inspection]
    Src --> CLI2[cli/ — CLI entry point]
    Src --> Device[device/ — ADB, simctl device discovery]
    Src --> Report[report/ — console, json, junit, html, allure, github reporters]
    Src --> Schemas[schemas/ — Element, Selector, DeviceInfo types]
```

---

## Drivers

All platform interaction in spana flows through the `RawDriverService` interface. Platform-specific drivers implement this interface as thin clients (HTTP for UiAutomator2 / WebDriverAgent / Appium, CDP or Playwright for browsers and desktop webviews). The core methods carry no selection logic, no auto-wait, no retry — just raw platform calls.

## RawDriverService interface

```ts
// Simplified — see src/drivers/raw-driver.ts for the full interface.
interface RawDriverService {
  dumpHierarchy(): Effect.Effect<RawHierarchy, DriverError>;
  tapAtCoordinate(x: number, y: number): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  doubleTapAtCoordinate(x: number, y: number): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  longPressAtCoordinate(x: number, y: number, duration: number): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  swipe(
    startX: number,
    startY: number,
    endX: number,
    endY: number,
    duration: number,
  ): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  inputText(text: string): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  pressKey(key: string): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  hideKeyboard(): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  takeScreenshot(): Effect.Effect<Uint8Array, DriverError>;
  getDeviceInfo(): Effect.Effect<DeviceInfo, DriverError>;
  launchApp(bundleId: string, opts?: LaunchOptions): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  stopApp(bundleId: string): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  killApp(bundleId: string): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  clearAppState(bundleId: string): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  openLink(url: string): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  back(): Effect.Effect<void, DriverError>;
  evaluate<T>(
    script: string | ((...args: any[]) => T),
    ...args: unknown[]
  ): Effect.Effect<T, DriverError>;

  // Optional capabilities (present only on drivers that support them):
  // pinch / zoom / multiTouch, webview contexts, domChannel, network mocking,
  // cookies / auth state, tabs, console logs / JS errors / HAR, WebAuthn virtual authenticator.
  domChannel?: DomChannel;
}
```

The Smart Layer (`coordinator.ts`, `auto-wait.ts`, `element-matcher.ts`, `channel-resolver.ts`) is the main consumer of this interface. Flow authors do not normally use it directly (the debug REPL exposes it as `driver`). The optional `domChannel` is the one place selectors reach a driver: web drivers and the in-app `spana-bridge` use it to resolve and act on elements inside the page.

## Driver architecture

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph CLI process [CLI process — Bun/TS]
        RD[RawDriverService]
    end

    subgraph Android
        UA2[UiAutomator2 APK server\nport 6790 on device\nADB-forwarded to host port 8200+]
    end

    subgraph iOS
        WDA[WebDriverAgent XCTest\nport 8100+\niproxy-forwarded on physical devices]
    end

    subgraph Web
        PW[Chromium\nPlaywright or direct CDP]
    end

    RD -- HTTP --> UA2
    RD -- HTTP --> WDA
    RD -. CDP .-> PW
```

## Web drivers (Playwright, direct CDP, Lightpanda)

The web engine is selected with `execution.web.engine` (`resolveWebEngine()` in `src/runtime/local.ts`):

| Engine                   | Driver                       | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"playwright"` (default) | `src/drivers/playwright.ts`  | Uses `playwright-core`. Supports `chromium`, `firefox`, `webkit`, `channel`, `wsEndpoint`, and HAR recording.                                                                                 |
| `"cdp"`                  | `src/drivers/cdp-browser.ts` | Launches Chromium itself (or attaches to `execution.web.cdpUrl`) and talks to it over a raw CDP WebSocket, with no Playwright client. Auto-attaches to cross-origin (out-of-process) iframes. |
| `"lightpanda"`           | `src/drivers/cdp-browser.ts` | Connects over CDP to an already-running Lightpanda server at `execution.web.cdpUrl` (default `http://127.0.0.1:9222`). spana does not start Lightpanda.                                       |
| `"auto"`                 | —                            | Picks `"cdp"` when the browser is Chromium and none of `wsEndpoint`, `channel`, or `artifacts.har` is set; otherwise `"playwright"`.                                                          |

- The `playwright` and `cdp` engines launch the browser (or attach to `cdpUrl` / `wsEndpoint`); all engines navigate to `apps.web.url` (default `http://localhost:3000`) and expose the page via the `RawDriverService` interface.
- `dumpHierarchy()` walks the DOM inside the page (`page.evaluate` on Playwright, `Runtime.evaluate` on CDP) and returns it as structured JSON.
- Coordinate taps are issued via `page.mouse.click(x, y)` on Playwright and `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` on CDP.
- Both drivers expose a DOM channel, so the Smart Layer can resolve selectors inside the page.

Desktop targets use the same web parser: Electron (`src/drivers/electron.ts`, Playwright `_electron` or CDP attach) and Electrobun (`src/drivers/electrobun.ts`, CDP or WebKit inspector).

## Android driver (UiAutomator2)

The Android driver is a pure HTTP client that talks to the UiAutomator2 APK server running on the device.

**Setup sequence** (`src/drivers/uiautomator2/installer.ts`):

1. spana installs the UiAutomator2 server and test APKs via ADB if they are not already on the device. The APKs come from the optional `appium-uiautomator2-server` dependency (or a local `drivers/android/` directory).
2. It starts the server on the device with `adb shell am instrument` (port 6790).
3. ADB port-forwarding maps device port 6790 to a local port (allocated from 8200).
4. The driver sends HTTP requests to `http://localhost:<forwarded-port>`.

With `execution.warmDaemons.enabled`, a healthy server from an earlier run is reused instead.

**Key endpoints** (all under `/session/:id`):

- `GET /source` — returns the full UI hierarchy as XML
- `POST /appium/gestures/click` — taps at coordinates
- `POST /appium/device/activate_app` — launches the app by package name

The driver parses the XML hierarchy in TypeScript and produces the unified `Element` tree. No XML parsing happens in the APK.

## iOS driver (WebDriverAgent)

The iOS driver is a pure HTTP client that talks to the WebDriverAgent (WDA) XCTest bundle running on the simulator or device.

spana finds the WDA Xcode project in the optional `appium-webdriveragent` dependency (or a local `drivers/ios/WebDriverAgent/` directory) and builds it with `xcodebuild` (`src/drivers/wda/installer.ts`).

**Simulator setup:**

1. On first use for a simulator, spana runs `xcodebuild build-for-testing` without code signing and caches the build in `.wda-builds/<udid>`.
2. It starts WDA with `xcodebuild test-without-building` on a port allocated from 8100.
3. The driver sends HTTP requests to `http://localhost:<port>`.

**Device setup:**

1. With `apps.ios.signing.teamId` set, spana builds WDA for the device with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` and `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY` (default `"Apple Development"`), then starts it.
2. `iproxy` (from `libimobiledevice`) forwards the device port to a local port.
3. The driver connects to the forwarded port.

Without `signing`, spana assumes WDA is already running on the device and only opens the `iproxy` tunnel.

**Key endpoints** (all under `/session/:id`):

- `GET /source` — returns the full accessibility tree as XML
- `POST /wda/tap` — taps at coordinates
- `POST /wda/apps/launch` — launches the app by bundle ID

## Hierarchy parsing

Each platform returns a different hierarchy format:

| Platform                    | Format                          | Parser location                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Android                     | XML (UiAutomator ViewHierarchy) | `src/drivers/uiautomator2/pagesource.ts` |
| iOS                         | XML (WDA accessibility tree)    | `src/drivers/wda/pagesource.ts`          |
| Web / Electron / Electrobun | JSON (in-page DOM walk)         | `src/drivers/playwright-parser.ts`       |

All parsers output the same unified `Element` type:

```ts
// Simplified from src/schemas/element.ts
interface Element {
  id?: string; // testID / resource-id / accessibility identifier
  text?: string;
  value?: string;
  accessibilityLabel?: string;
  resourceId?: string;
  elementType?: string;
  bounds: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };
  enabled?: boolean;
  visible?: boolean;
  clickable?: boolean;
  focused?: boolean;
  attributes?: Record<string, string>;
  children?: Element[];
}
```

`element-matcher.ts` in the Smart Layer searches this tree for the selector — no platform-specific code required.

## Inspiration

The thin HTTP client approach used by the WDA and UiAutomator2 drivers was inspired by [maestro-runner](https://github.com/nicklassuperset/maestro-runner), a Go project that demonstrated how minimal HTTP clients can effectively drive device interaction without heavy abstractions. The web drivers follow a similar philosophy: the `cdp` engine speaks raw CDP over a WebSocket, and the `playwright` engine calls Playwright directly rather than wrapping it in additional layers.

---

## Device Setup

Spana auto-discovers available devices for each platform. This guide covers how to set up and verify your devices before running tests.

## Checking available devices

```bash
spana devices
```

This lists discovered devices for all platforms (web, Electron, Electrobun, Android, iOS) as platform, name, type, and state:

```
  web         Chromium (Playwright)                browser    available
  electron    Electron (Playwright _electron / CDP) desktop    available
  electrobun  Electrobun (Native WebView / CEF)    desktop    available
  android     emulator-5554                        emulator   device
  ios         iPhone 16 (iOS.18.4)                 simulator  Booted
  ios         iPhone 16 Pro (iOS.18.4)             simulator  Shutdown
```

For Android, the name is the serial you pass to `--device`. The plain output does not show iOS UDIDs: use `spana devices --json` to get each device's `id`.

## Web

Web testing uses a local Chromium by default. Install a Playwright browser once (`npx playwright install chromium`), or point `execution.web.executablePath` (or `execution.web.channel` on the `playwright` engine) at an installed browser. The `cdp` engine falls back to a system Chrome when no Playwright Chromium is found. `spana doctor` checks this for you.

Spana always shows `playwright-chromium` as an available web device. The browser engine (`execution.web.engine`: `"playwright"` default, `"cdp"`, `"lightpanda"`, or `"auto"`) is chosen in config, not by device.

## Android

Spana discovers Android devices through `adb` (Android Debug Bridge).

### Prerequisites

- **Android SDK** -- install via [Android Studio](https://developer.android.com/studio) or the command-line tools
- **ADB** -- included in the Android SDK platform tools
- **Java 17+** -- required by UiAutomator2

### Using an emulator

In a single-device run (no `--parallel` / `--workers` / `--devices`), if no device or emulator is connected, spana boots the first AVD from `emulator -list-avds` for you. To start one yourself:

```bash
# List available AVDs
emulator -list-avds

# Start an emulator
emulator -avd Pixel_7_API_34 &

# Verify it appears
adb devices
# emulator-5554   device
```

### Using a physical device

1. Enable **Developer Options** on the device
2. Enable **USB Debugging** in Developer Options
3. Connect via USB and accept the debugging prompt
4. Verify: `adb devices` should show your device serial

### Targeting a specific device

When multiple Android devices are connected:

```bash
# Use the --device flag with the serial from `spana devices`
spana test --platform android --device emulator-5554
```

## iOS

Spana discovers iOS simulators through Xcode's `simctl` (all available simulators, booted or not) and connected physical devices through `xcrun devicectl` (Xcode 15+).

When you do not pass `--device`, spana tries a connected physical device first and falls back to a simulator. It prefers a simulator that already has your app installed (booted first), then any booted simulator, then the first available one, and boots it if needed. Boot a simulator before you target it with `--device`.

### Prerequisites

- **Xcode** -- install from the Mac App Store
- **Xcode Command Line Tools** -- `xcode-select --install`
- **WebDriverAgent** -- spana builds it with `xcodebuild` from the optional `appium-webdriveragent` dependency on first use per simulator

### Booting a simulator

```bash
# List all available simulators
xcrun simctl list devices available

# Boot a simulator
xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 16"

# Or open the Simulator app
open -a Simulator
```

### Targeting a specific simulator

```bash
# Use the UDID from `spana devices --json`
spana test --platform ios --device 7338EC82-D2BD-4722-B148-D009FDA64F6E
```

### Physical iOS devices

Physical iOS devices need `iproxy` (`brew install libimobiledevice`) and a signed WebDriverAgent. Add your team ID so spana can build and sign WDA for the device:

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  apps: {
    ios: {
      bundleId: "com.example.myapp",
      signing: {
        teamId: "YOUR_TEAM_ID",
        signingIdentity: "Apple Development", // optional, this is the default
      },
    },
  },
});
```

`signing` accepts only `teamId` and `signingIdentity`. Without `signing`, spana expects WebDriverAgent to already be running on the device and only opens the `iproxy` tunnel.

## Multi-device testing

Run the same flows on multiple devices simultaneously. `--device` takes a single ID; use `--devices` (comma-separated) or `--parallel` for more than one:

```bash
# Run on a specific Android and iOS device
spana test --devices emulator-5554,7338EC82-D2BD-4722-B148-D009FDA64F6E

# Auto-discover all devices and run in parallel (cap with --workers <n>)
spana test --platform android,ios --parallel
```

With `--devices`, platforms are inferred from the selected devices when `--platform` is not set. `--devices` cannot be combined with `--device`.

When none of `--device`, `--devices`, `--parallel`, or `--workers` is provided, spana uses one device per platform, chosen as described above.

## Troubleshooting

### Android: "no devices found"

- Check `adb devices` shows your device with state `device` (not `offline` or `unauthorized`)
- Restart ADB: `adb kill-server && adb start-server`
- For emulators, ensure the emulator is fully booted (wait for the home screen)

### iOS: "No iOS simulator or physical device available"

- Check that at least one simulator is available: `xcrun simctl list devices available`
- If none is listed, create one in Xcode (Settings > Platforms / Devices and Simulators)
- To skip the boot wait, boot one first: `xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 16"`

### iOS: WebDriverAgent build fails

- Check that `appium-webdriveragent` is installed (it is an optional dependency), or place WDA in `drivers/ios/WebDriverAgent/`
- Open `WebDriverAgent.xcodeproj` in Xcode and resolve signing issues
- Ensure your Xcode version matches the simulator runtime
- Try: `xcodebuild -showsdks` to verify available SDKs

---

## Remote Execution

By default, spana runs tests locally using built-in drivers (Playwright or direct CDP for web, UiAutomator2 for Android, WebDriverAgent for iOS). Switch to **Appium mode** to run Android and iOS against a remote Appium server — useful for cloud device farms, shared test infrastructure, or devices on another machine. Web, Electron, and Electrobun still run locally in Appium mode.

## Enabling Appium mode

### Config file

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      serverUrl: "http://localhost:4723",
    },
  },
});
```

### CLI flags

```bash
spana test --appium-url http://localhost:4723
```

The `--appium-url` flag automatically enables Appium mode. You can also select the mode explicitly with `--driver appium` (or `--driver local` to override a config that sets `mode: "appium"`).

The server URL is resolved in this order: `--appium-url`, the `SPANA_APPIUM_URL` environment variable, then `execution.appium.serverUrl`. `SPANA_APPIUM_URL` only supplies the URL; it does not switch on Appium mode by itself.

### Auto-starting a local Appium server

With `--appium-auto-start` (or `execution.appium.autoStart: true`), spana spawns `appium` from `PATH` for the duration of the run and ignores any configured URL. Appium mode must still be on (`mode: "appium"` or `--driver appium`). Use `autoStartBinary` and `autoStartArgs` to change the binary or pass extra arguments.

## How it works

In Appium mode, spana:

1. Connects to the Appium server at the given URL
2. Creates one session per platform with the resolved [capabilities](#capabilities)
3. Runs your flows using the Appium WebDriver protocol instead of local drivers
4. Deletes the session when the run completes
5. Reports results to the [cloud provider](/guides/cloud-providers) if detected

The same flow files work in both local and Appium mode -- no changes needed.

Appium mode runs one session per platform. `--parallel`, `--workers`, and `--devices` use the local device-discovery path and do not create Appium sessions.

## Cloud helper config

For BrowserStack and Sauce Labs, Spana can also manage provider-specific helper behavior on top of raw capabilities:

- upload a local app artifact and inject `appium:app`
- start and stop BrowserStack Local / Sauce Connect
- fill missing `bstack:options` / `sauce:options` values from config

Raw capabilities still win. Helper config fills missing provider fields and lifecycle, but it does not override explicit `appium:app`, `bstack:options`, or `sauce:options` values you already provided through config, `--caps`, or `--caps-json`.

## Capabilities

Appium sessions are configured through W3C capabilities. Spana merges capabilities from five sources (later overrides earlier):

| Source              | How to set                                               | Example                                |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Launch device state | `launchOptions.deviceState`                              | `{ language: "sv", locale: "sv_SE" }`  |
| Config file         | `execution.appium.capabilities`                          | `{ "appium:app": "/path/to/app" }`     |
| Platform config     | `execution.appium.platformCapabilities.android` / `.ios` | `{ "appium:deviceName": "iPhone 15" }` |
| JSON file           | `--caps <path>` or `capabilitiesFile` in config          | `caps.json`                            |
| Inline CLI          | `--caps-json '<json>'`                                   | `'{"appium:deviceName": "Pixel 7"}'`   |

### Android capabilities

```json title="caps-android.json"
{
  "appium:automationName": "UiAutomator2",
  "appium:deviceName": "emulator-5554",
  "appium:app": "/path/to/app.apk",
  "appium:appPackage": "com.example.myapp",
  "appium:appActivity": "com.example.myapp.MainActivity"
}
```

Spana sets `platformName: "Android"` by default. Your capabilities can override it.

### iOS capabilities

```json title="caps-ios.json"
{
  "appium:automationName": "XCUITest",
  "appium:deviceName": "iPhone 15",
  "appium:platformVersion": "18.0",
  "appium:app": "/path/to/app.ipa",
  "appium:bundleId": "com.example.myapp"
}
```

Spana sets `platformName: "iOS"` and `appium:automationName: "XCUITest"` by default. Your capabilities can override them.

## Local Appium server

To test against a local Appium server:

```bash
# Install Appium
npm install -g appium

# Install drivers
appium driver install uiautomator2
appium driver install xcuitest

# Start the server
appium

# Run tests against it
spana test --appium-url http://localhost:4723
```

## Config reference

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      // Appium server URL (required in appium mode)
      serverUrl: "http://localhost:4723",

      // Inline capabilities (applied after launchOptions.deviceState)
      capabilities: {
        "appium:app": "/path/to/app.apk",
      },

      // Per-platform capabilities (override `capabilities`)
      platformCapabilities: {
        android: { "appium:deviceName": "Pixel 7" },
        ios: { "appium:deviceName": "iPhone 15" },
      },

      // Path to a JSON capabilities file, resolved relative to spana.config.ts
      // (overrides config capabilities; --caps-json overrides this)
      capabilitiesFile: "./caps.json",

      // Report results to cloud provider (default: true)
      reportToProvider: true,

      // Spawn a local `appium` for the run (default: false)
      autoStart: false,
      autoStartBinary: "appium",
      autoStartArgs: [],

      // Custom cloud provider module (see Cloud Providers guide)
      // cloudProvider: "./providers/acme-grid.ts",

      // BrowserStack helper config
      browserstack: {
        app: { path: "./builds/app.apk", customId: "spana-android" },
        local: { enabled: true, identifier: "spana-local" },
        options: {
          projectName: "my-app",
          buildName: "ci-42",
        },
      },

      // Sauce Labs helper config
      saucelabs: {
        app: { path: "./builds/app.apk", name: "app.apk" },
        connect: { enabled: true, tunnelName: "spana-ci" },
        options: {
          build: "ci-42",
          name: "login-flow",
        },
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## CLI flags

| Flag                       | Description                             |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `--appium-url <url>`       | Appium server URL (enables appium mode) |
| `--driver <local\|appium>` | Select the execution mode explicitly    |
| `--appium-auto-start`      | Spawn a local `appium` for the run      |
| `--caps <path>`            | Path to capabilities JSON file          |
| `--caps-json <json>`       | Inline capabilities JSON string         |
| `--no-provider-reporting`  | Disable cloud provider result reporting |

## Cloud providers

When the Appium URL points to BrowserStack or Sauce Labs, spana auto-detects the provider and reports test results. See the [Cloud Providers](/guides/cloud-providers) guide for setup details.

---

## Cloud Providers

Spana can run mobile (Android and iOS) tests on cloud device farms through Appium. It auto-detects BrowserStack and Sauce Labs from the server URL hostname, reports the run result back to the provider dashboard, and can manage provider-specific upload/tunnel helpers from config. Keep the credentials in the URL (`https://USER:KEY@...`): managed uploads, tunnels, and result reporting read them from there.

## Supported providers

| Provider                          | Auto-detected | Result reporting | Managed helpers           |
| --------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| BrowserStack                      | Yes           | Yes              | Yes                       |
| Sauce Labs                        | Yes           | Yes              | Yes                       |
| Custom provider (`cloudProvider`) | --            | No (see below)   | Yes (your `createHelper`) |
| Other Appium grid                 | --            | No               | No                        |

## BrowserStack

### 1. Set your credentials

Embed credentials in the Appium server URL:

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      serverUrl: "https://USER:KEY@hub-cloud.browserstack.com/wd/hub",
    },
  },
});
```

Or pass them on the CLI:

```bash
spana test --appium-url "https://USER:KEY@hub-cloud.browserstack.com/wd/hub"
```

### 2. Set capabilities or helper config

Create a `caps.json` file with BrowserStack-specific options:

```json title="caps.json"
{
  "bstack:options": {
    "projectName": "my-app",
    "buildName": "ci-42",
    "deviceName": "Samsung Galaxy S23",
    "os_version": "13.0"
  },
  "appium:app": "bs://app-id-from-upload"
}
```

Then reference it:

```bash
spana test --caps caps.json
```

Or let Spana manage app upload, BrowserStack Local, and default `bstack:options` values from config:

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  apps: {
    android: {
      packageName: "com.example.myapp",
      appPath: "./builds/app.apk",
    },
  },
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      serverUrl: "https://USER:KEY@hub-cloud.browserstack.com/wd/hub",
      browserstack: {
        app: {
          customId: "spana-android",
        },
        local: {
          enabled: true,
          identifier: "spana-local",
        },
        options: {
          projectName: "my-app",
          buildName: process.env.CI_BUILD_ID ?? "local",
        },
      },
      capabilities: {
        "appium:deviceName": "Samsung Galaxy S23",
        "appium:platformVersion": "13.0",
      },
    },
  },
});
```

When an `execution.appium.browserstack` block is present, Spana uploads `browserstack.app.path`, or `apps.<platform>.appPath` when that is not set, and injects the returned `bs://...` URL as `appium:app`. Use `browserstack.app.id` when you already have a `bs://...` reference. If `appium:app` or `bstack:options` are already set in raw capabilities, those explicit values win and helper config only fills what is missing.

### 3. Result reporting

Spana reports pass/fail status to BrowserStack once, after the whole run completes. This updates each Appium session in the BrowserStack dashboard with the name `spana <platforms>` and `passed` (no flow failed) or `failed`. No per-flow status or failure reason is sent.

Disable reporting with `--no-provider-reporting` or in config:

```ts
appium: {
  reportToProvider: false,
}
```

When `browserstack.local.enabled` is true, Spana starts and stops BrowserStack Local for the run. Set `browserstack.local.binary` if the `BrowserStackLocal` binary is not on `PATH`, or keep managing the tunnel yourself and pass `bstack:options.local` manually.

## Sauce Labs

### 1. Set your credentials

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      serverUrl: "https://USER:KEY@ondemand.us-west-1.saucelabs.com/wd/hub",
    },
  },
});
```

For EU data center:

```bash
spana test --appium-url "https://USER:KEY@ondemand.eu-central-1.saucelabs.com/wd/hub"
```

### 2. Set capabilities or helper config

```json title="caps.json"
{
  "sauce:options": {
    "name": "login-flow",
    "build": "ci-42",
    "appiumVersion": "2.0"
  },
  "appium:deviceName": "Google Pixel 7",
  "appium:platformVersion": "13",
  "appium:app": "storage:filename=app.apk"
}
```

Or let Spana manage Sauce storage uploads, Sauce Connect, and default `sauce:options` values from config:

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  apps: {
    android: {
      packageName: "com.example.myapp",
      appPath: "./builds/app.apk",
    },
  },
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      serverUrl: "https://USER:KEY@ondemand.us-west-1.saucelabs.com/wd/hub",
      saucelabs: {
        app: {
          name: "app.apk",
        },
        connect: {
          enabled: true,
          tunnelName: "spana-ci",
        },
        options: {
          build: process.env.CI_BUILD_ID ?? "local",
          name: "login-flow",
        },
      },
      capabilities: {
        "appium:deviceName": "Google Pixel 7",
        "appium:platformVersion": "13",
      },
    },
  },
});
```

When an `execution.appium.saucelabs` block is present, Spana uploads `saucelabs.app.path`, or `apps.<platform>.appPath` when that is not set, to Sauce storage and injects `storage:<id>` as `appium:app`. Use `saucelabs.app.id` when you already have a Sauce storage reference such as `storage:YOUR_APP_ID`. Explicit `appium:app` and `sauce:options` capability values still override helper-derived defaults.

### 3. Result reporting

Sauce Labs sessions are updated with pass/fail status once, after the whole run completes (same rules as BrowserStack). Region is detected from the server URL hostname: uploads and Sauce Connect use `eu-central`, `us-east`, or `us-west` (default); result reporting uses `eu-central-1` when the hostname contains `eu-central`, otherwise `us-west-1`.

When `saucelabs.connect.enabled` is true, Spana starts and stops Sauce Connect for the run. Set `saucelabs.connect.binary` if the `sc` binary is not on `PATH`, or keep managing the tunnel yourself and pass `sauce:options.tunnelName` manually.

## Capability resolution

Capabilities merge from five sources, with later sources overriding earlier ones (`src/runtime/capabilities.ts`):

1. **Launch device state** -- `launchOptions.deviceState` (`language` / `locale` / `timeZone`) mapped to Appium capabilities
2. **Config file** -- `execution.appium.capabilities` in `spana.config.ts`
3. **Platform-specific config** -- `execution.appium.platformCapabilities.android` or `.ios`, for the platform being run
4. **Capabilities file** -- `--caps <path>` flag or `execution.appium.capabilitiesFile` in config
5. **Inline CLI JSON** -- `--caps-json '{"key": "value"}'`

This lets you keep shared capabilities in config, platform or environment-specific ones in `platformCapabilities` or a file, and override individual values from the CLI. Cloud helper config is applied after this merge and only fills fields that are still missing.

## Custom cloud providers

If you use an Appium grid other than BrowserStack or Sauce Labs, point `execution.appium.cloudProvider` at a module that default-exports a `CloudProvider`.

```ts title="spana.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  execution: {
    mode: "appium",
    appium: {
      serverUrl: "https://grid.example.com/wd/hub",
      cloudProvider: "./providers/acme-grid.ts",
    },
  },
});
```

The module path is resolved relative to `spana.config.ts`.

:::caution
Today the CLI only calls `createHelper()` (and the helper's `prepareCapabilities()` / `cleanup()`) on a custom provider. End-of-run result reporting is only wired for the built-in BrowserStack and Sauce Labs providers, so a custom `extractMeta()` / `reportResult()` is not called by `spana test`.
:::

### `CloudProvider`

```ts
import type { CloudProvider, CloudProviderHelper } from "spana-test";

const provider: CloudProvider = {
  name() {
    return "Acme Grid";
  },

  createHelper(appiumUrl, config): CloudProviderHelper {
    return {
      async prepareCapabilities(platform, caps, appConfig) {
        return {
          ...caps,
          "acme:options": {
            platform,
            appIdentifier: appConfig?.packageName ?? appConfig?.bundleId,
          },
        };
      },

      async cleanup() {
        // stop tunnels, delete temporary uploads, etc.
      },
    };
  },

  extractMeta(sessionId, caps, meta) {
    meta.sessionId = sessionId;
    meta.build = String(caps["build"] ?? "");
  },

  async reportResult(appiumUrl, meta, result) {
    await fetch(`${appiumUrl}/custom-results/${meta.sessionId}`, {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify(result),
    });
  },
};

export default provider;
```

### Interface responsibilities

| API                     | Responsibility                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name()`                | Human-readable provider name                                                                  |
| `createHelper()`        | Build a helper for capability mutation and lifecycle cleanup                                  |
| `prepareCapabilities()` | Add provider-specific desired capabilities before session creation                            |
| `cleanup()`             | Tear down uploads, tunnels, or temporary state after the run                                  |
| `extractMeta()`         | Pull provider metadata from the created session for reporting (built-in providers only today) |
| `reportResult()`        | Mark the remote session passed or failed (built-in providers only today)                      |

## CI example

```yaml title=".github/workflows/test.yml"
jobs:
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      - run: bun install
      - run: |
          spana test \
            --platform android \
            --appium-url "https://${{ secrets.BS_USER }}:${{ secrets.BS_KEY }}@hub-cloud.browserstack.com/wd/hub" \
            --caps caps.json \
            --caps-json '{"bstack:options": {"buildName": "${{ github.run_id }}"}}'
```

---

## CI/CD Integration

spana is designed for CI from the ground up. It ships as a single npm package (`spana-test`), produces machine-readable output via JSON and JUnit reporters, and uses standard exit codes so your pipeline can react to results without parsing logs.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`  | No flow failed. This includes runs where no flows matched, `--changed-since` filtered out every flow, or a platform was skipped because no device was found. |
| `1`  | At least one flow failed, or the command could not start (invalid options, a config that fails to load, missing Appium URL).                                 |

## Reporters for CI

Use the `--reporter` flag to control output format. Multiple reporters can be combined with commas.

```bash
# Machine-readable results for CI dashboards
spana test --reporter json,junit

# Human-readable HTML report for review
spana test --reporter html

# Combined: console output + JUnit + HTML
spana test --reporter console,junit,html
```

- **`junit`** — writes a JUnit XML file to `spana-output/junit-report.xml`, understood by most CI systems.
- **`json`** — prints one JSON event per line to stdout (`flowPass`, `flowFail`, `runComplete`), useful for piping to other tools.
- **`html`** — writes an HTML report to `spana-output/report.html` with screenshots and step details.
- **`allure`** — writes Allure result files for an Allure report.
- **`github`** — writes a PR-ready Markdown summary (`spana-output/github-pr-summary.md`) and appends directly to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in GitHub Actions.

The output directory is `artifacts.outputDir` (default `./spana-output`). Per-flow artifacts (screenshots, `hierarchy.json`, `failure-bundle.json`) go in `spana-output/<flow>-<platform>/`.

## PR-Aware CI Filtering (`--changed-since`)

Run only the flows affected by a pull request while staying **fail-open**. `--changed-since <ref>` diffs against `git merge-base <ref> HEAD` and runs the `filters` from `spana.config.ts` in order.

`--changed-since` does nothing without a `filters` list in config: spana prints a warning and runs all flows. If git fails (for example, the base ref is missing in a shallow clone), spana also fails open and runs all flows. If one filter throws, that filter is skipped and keeps every flow it received (flows an earlier filter excluded stay excluded). If the filters exclude every flow, the run exits `0`.

Built-in filters (all exported from `spana-test`):

- **`pathRuleFilter`** — deterministic, no LLM. Maps flow tags or file prefixes to watched source paths. Flows that no rule owns always run.
- **`deterministicImpactFilter`** — deterministic, no LLM. Uses path mappings and the import graph; by default, unmapped changes run everything.
- **`decisionFilter`** — asks a model judge (`createLogprobDecisionJudge` or `createOllamaDecisionJudge`) how likely each flow is affected, and skips flows below `threshold` (default `0.20`).

All three always keep changed flow files and flows with `alwaysRunTags`, and run everything when `spana.config.*` or a lockfile changes or a `runAllOnPaths` prefix matches. `decisionFilter` also runs everything when the diff exceeds `maxDiffBytes` (default 60 kB) and keeps a flow when the judge errors.

```ts
// spana.config.ts
import {
  defineConfig,
  decisionFilter,
  createLogprobDecisionJudge,
  pathRuleFilter,
} from "spana-test";

export default defineConfig({
  filters: [
    pathRuleFilter({
      rules: [{ matchFlow: { tag: "billing" }, watchPaths: ["src/billing/"] }],
    }),
    decisionFilter({
      alwaysRunTags: ["smoke"],
      judge: createLogprobDecisionJudge({
        provider: "openai", // works with vLLM, SGLang, llama-server, Typesafe AI, OpenRouter, or "ollama"
        baseUrl: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1",
        model: "typesafe-ai/jev",
      }),
    }),
  ],
});
```

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0 # required for merge-base diffing

- name: Run affected E2E flows
  run: >-
    npx spana test
    --parallel --workers 4
    --reporter console,junit,github
    ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('--changed-since origin/{0}', github.base_ref) || '' }}
```

`createLogprobDecisionJudge` places the shared git diff prefix **first** in every prompt so vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp can reuse the KV cache across every flow in the PR. It requests a single token (`YES` / `NO`) with `logprobs` and turns the top logprobs into a probability.

Spana also persists per-flow durations in `spana-output/.spana/last-run.json`. On later runs, multi-worker runs (`--parallel` / `--workers` / `--devices`) schedule the slowest flows first (`orderFlowsLongestFirst`), and `--shard` uses the durations to balance shards. Cache this file between CI runs to keep the benefit.

## GitHub Actions

### Using the reusable action

The spana repository contains a composite GitHub Action (`.github/actions/spana-test`) that handles installation, test execution, and artifact upload. The examples below reference it as a local action, so copy it into your repository first:

```yaml
name: E2E Tests

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  e2e-web:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run dev &
      - run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000

      - name: Run E2E tests
        uses: ./.github/actions/spana-test
        with:
          platform: web
          reporters: console,junit,html

  e2e-android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Set up Android emulator
        uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 33
          script: echo "Emulator ready"

      - name: Run E2E tests
        uses: ./.github/actions/spana-test
        with:
          platform: android
          retries: 1

  e2e-ios:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - run: npm ci

      - name: Boot iOS Simulator
        run: |
          xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 15"
          xcrun simctl bootstatus "iPhone 15" -b

      - name: Run E2E tests
        uses: ./.github/actions/spana-test
        with:
          platform: ios
```

#### Action inputs

| Input               | Default              | Description                                               |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `platform`          | `web`                | Platform to test (web, android, ios)                      |
| `reporters`         | `console,junit,html` | Comma-separated reporter names                            |
| `config`            | —                    | Path to spana.config.ts                                   |
| `flow-path`         | —                    | Path to flow files or directory                           |
| `device`            | —                    | Target a specific device by ID                            |
| `retries`           | —                    | Number of retries for failed flows                        |
| `tags`              | —                    | Filter by tags                                            |
| `grep`              | —                    | Filter by name pattern                                    |
| `working-directory` | `.`                  | Directory to run spana in                                 |
| `version`           | `latest`             | `spana-test` version to install                           |
| `upload-artifacts`  | `true`               | Upload `spana-output/` and `allure-results/` as artifacts |

The action also sets a `result` output (`pass` or `fail`).

### Manual workflow setup

If you prefer full control over the workflow steps:

```yaml
name: E2E Tests (Web)

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  e2e-web:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install spana
        run: npm install -g spana-test

      - name: Install Chromium
        run: npx playwright install chromium

      - name: Start app
        run: npm run dev &

      - name: Wait for app
        run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000

      - name: Run tests
        run: spana test --platform web --reporter console,junit,html

      - name: Upload JUnit results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-results
          path: spana-output/junit-report.xml

      - name: Upload HTML report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: html-report
          path: spana-output/report.html

      - name: Upload per-flow artifacts (screenshots, hierarchy, failure bundles)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: spana-output
          path: spana-output/
```

### Android tests

Android tests need the Android SDK. GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runners include the SDK, but you need to boot an emulator.

```yaml
e2e-android:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: 24

    - name: Install spana
      run: npm install -g spana-test

    - name: Set up Android emulator
      uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
      with:
        api-level: 33
        script: |
          adb wait-for-device
          spana test --platform android --reporter console,junit,html

    - name: Upload test artifacts
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: android-results
        path: spana-output/
```

### iOS tests

iOS tests require a macOS runner with Xcode installed.

```yaml
e2e-ios:
  runs-on: macos-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: 24

    - name: Install spana
      run: npm install -g spana-test

    - name: Boot iOS Simulator
      run: |
        xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 15"
        xcrun simctl bootstatus "iPhone 15" -b

    - name: Install app and run tests
      run: spana test --platform ios --reporter console,junit,html

    - name: Upload test artifacts
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: ios-results
        path: spana-output/
```

## GitLab CI

```yaml
e2e-web:
  image: node:20
  stage: test
  script:
    - npm ci
    - npm install -g spana-test
    - npm run dev &
    - npx wait-on http://localhost:3000
    - spana test --platform web --reporter console,junit,html
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - spana-output/
    reports:
      junit: spana-output/junit-report.xml
```

GitLab natively parses JUnit XML when declared under `artifacts.reports.junit`, so test results appear directly in merge request widgets.

## Tips

- **Combine reporters.** Use `--reporter console,junit,html` to get terminal output for logs, JUnit for CI dashboards, and HTML for manual review — all in one run.
- **Upload `spana-output/` as artifacts.** This directory contains JUnit XML, HTML reports, and per-flow screenshots, hierarchies, and failure bundles. Always upload with `if: always()` (GitHub Actions) or `when: always` (GitLab) so artifacts are available even when tests fail.
- **Headless web works out of the box.** Web runs are headless by default (`execution.web.headless`). No `xvfb` or display server setup needed. Install a browser on the runner first (`npx playwright install chromium`). The `playwright` engine needs it; the `cdp` engine uses it when present and otherwise falls back to a system Chrome.
- **Pick a web engine.** `execution.web.engine` accepts `"playwright"` (default), `"cdp"`, `"lightpanda"`, or `"auto"`. `"auto"` uses the direct CDP engine for Chromium unless `wsEndpoint`, `channel`, or `artifacts.har` needs Playwright.
- **Scale web workers.** `--workers <n>` runs `n` isolated browser contexts, spread over browser processes by `execution.web.maxContextsPerBrowser`.
- **Split across jobs.** `--shard <current>/<total>` runs one slice of the flows per CI job.
- **Use tags to split pipelines.** Run `spana test --tag smoke` on every push and `spana test --tag regression` on a nightly schedule to balance speed and coverage.
- **Pin spana version.** Use `npm install -g spana-test@<version>` (for example `spana-test@0.7.0`) in CI to avoid unexpected breakage from new releases.

---

## Debugging

When a test fails, spana can drop you into an interactive REPL connected to the live device session. This lets you inspect the screen, try selectors, and experiment with actions before the session is torn down.

## Enabling the debug REPL

```bash
spana test --debug-on-failure
```

When a flow fails, instead of moving to the next flow, spana pauses and opens a REPL:

```
Entering debug REPL for failed flow "login flow" on android.
Available bindings: app, expect, driver, platform, flowName, error, hierarchy(), selectors(), help()
Use top-level await for async calls, for example: await app.tap({ text: "Login" })

spana:android>
```

## Available bindings

| Binding       | Type     | Description                                          |
| ------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `app`         | object   | Full `PromiseApp` API -- tap, inputText, scroll, etc |
| `expect`      | function | Assertion helper, same as in flows                   |
| `driver`      | object   | Raw driver service for low-level access              |
| `platform`    | string   | Current platform (`"web"`, `"android"`, `"ios"`)     |
| `flowName`    | string   | Name of the failed flow                              |
| `error`       | Error    | The error that caused the failure                    |
| `hierarchy()` | async    | Returns the parsed UI element tree                   |
| `selectors()` | async    | Returns suggested selectors for visible elements     |
| `help()`      | function | Print all available bindings                         |

## Example session

```
spana:android> error.message
'Timed out waiting for selector { testID: "welcome-text" }'

spana:android> await selectors()
[
  { suggestedSelector: { testID: 'login-button' }, elementType: 'Button', text: 'Sign In' },
  { suggestedSelector: { text: 'Welcome' }, elementType: 'Text', text: 'Welcome' },
  ...
]

spana:android> await app.tap({ text: "Sign In" })
undefined

spana:android> await expect({ testID: "welcome-text" }).toBeVisible()
undefined

spana:android> .exit
```

## Tips

- Use `await selectors()` to discover what's on screen -- this is the fastest way to find the right selector
- Use `await hierarchy()` for the full element tree with bounds, visibility, and nesting
- All `app` methods use auto-wait, so `await app.tap(...)` will retry until the element appears
- The REPL only activates once per test run (the first failure) to avoid blocking CI
- The REPL requires an interactive terminal (TTY on both stdin and stdout) -- it's skipped automatically when there is none, as in most CI environments
- Type `.exit` or press `Ctrl+D` to leave the REPL and continue the test run

## Failure artifacts and `--verbose`

Every failed flow writes artifacts to `spana-output/<flow>-<platform>/` (by default `artifacts.captureOnFailure` is on): a screenshot, `hierarchy.json`, and `failure-bundle.json` with the failing selector and nearby alternatives. Web runs also capture console logs and JS errors (`artifacts.consoleLogs` / `artifacts.jsErrors`, on by default).

Pass `--verbose` to print the failure category, message, suggestion, diagnostic sections, and stack trace in the terminal:

```bash
spana test --verbose
```

## Visual Playback & Video Recording

Enable visual playback or video recording in `spana.config.ts` so anyone can visually scrub through every step in `report.html` (Play/Pause, 0.5×/1×/2× speed, timeline scrubber, red click-ripple indicator, synchronized step list, and embedded `<video>`). Both are off by default:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  artifacts: {
    playback: true, // Interactive timeline player in report.html
    video: "retain-on-failure", // "off" (default) | "on" | "retain-on-failure"
  },
  reporters: ["console", "html"],
});
```

How video is captured depends on the target:

- **Web** -- CDP screencast (`Page.startScreencast`). This needs the direct CDP engine (`execution.web.engine: "cdp"`, or `"auto"` when it resolves to `cdp`). The frames are muxed to `.mp4` only when `ffmpeg` is on `PATH`.
- **Android** -- `adb shell screenrecord`.
- **iOS Simulator** -- `xcrun simctl io <udid> recordVideo`.

Where no screencast is available (for example the `playwright` web engine), `playback: true` builds the timeline from step screenshots, so also set `artifacts.captureSteps: true`.

## Common Pitfalls Spana Protects Against & How to Fix Your App

Spana catches both test flakiness and real application bugs. When a test fails, fix the root cause rather than adding `sleep()` calls:

| Pitfall                                             | How Spana protects you automatically                                                                                                                                                               | Recommended fix in your app or config                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hydration / loading overlay swallows clicks**     | Single-RTT in-page actionability verifies the target is visible, enabled, unobstructed via deep `elementFromPoint`, and stable for 2 animation frames before tapping.                              | Expose `window.__SPANA_APP_READY__ = true` once your SPA finishes initial hydration/auth boot; Spana automatically waits for it before interacting.                        |
| **Stale async fetches clobber UI state**            | Fast Direct CDP interactions can expose out-of-order `fetch()` responses when users switch tabs or type rapidly.                                                                                   | Guard async UI updates with an `AbortController` or monotonic request sequence ID (`if (seq !== latestSeq) return`) in your app components.                                |
| **Missing or brittle selectors**                    | Failure bundles list the exact attempted selector plus nearby visible alternatives.                                                                                                                | Add stable `data-testid` / `testID` attributes to interactive elements instead of matching localized copy or fragile CSS paths.                                            |
| **Cross-origin `<iframe>` (Stripe, OAuth)**         | With the direct CDP engine (`engine: "cdp"` or `"auto"`), Spana auto-attaches to out-of-process iframes (`Target.setAutoAttach`) and translates element coordinates into top-level viewport space. | Ensure elements inside your own embedded frames expose `data-testid` or accessible labels.                                                                                 |
| **Flaky animations & layout shift**                 | 2-rAF stability check waits for moving buttons to settle before clicking.                                                                                                                          | Enable `execution.web.instantAnimations: true` in `spana.config.ts` to collapse CSS transitions to 0.001 ms during E2E runs.                                               |
| **Accessibility regressions**                       | `await expect().toPassAccessibilityAudit()` (and `spana_assert_accessible` in MCP) runs `axe-core` and reports WCAG rules, severity, and offending nodes.                                          | Fix missing `aria-label`, heading order, color contrast, and form `<label>` associations directly in the component rather than disabling rules.                            |
| **Visual diff noise from timestamps/avatars**       | `toMatchScreenshot()` (Rust-accelerated when the native library is available) supports dynamic region masks and a `layout-tolerant` compare mode.                                                  | Pass `{ mask: [{ testID: "live-clock" }] }` to `toMatchScreenshot()`, set `visualRegression.mode: "layout-tolerant"` in config, or freeze clock/seed data in your fixture. |
| **Slow repeated UI login & cross-test state leaks** | `freshContextPerFlow: true` isolates cookies/storage per flow while pre-warming the next context in the background.                                                                                | Use `definePersona()` + `PersonaAuthCache` or `createApiFixture()` to seed state via API instead of clicking through login in every test.                                  |
